governed_construct: A client-side local/offline data store used to persist application data in the unit: instantiation of a local database or storage handle (e.g. `new X(...)` of a storage library, `openDB(...)`, `indexedDB.open(...)`, `localforage.createInstance(...)`, a `Dexie` subclass) or direct read/write calls to a browser persistence API (`localStorage.setItem/getItem`, idb-keyval `get/set`). Each such store or persistence call is one instance.
interpretation: The rule asks that offline data be stored with PouchDB. An instance conforms when the store is a PouchDB database, i.e. it is created with a constructor bound (by resolving the import or require) to the default export of `pouchdb`, `pouchdb-browser`, `pouchdb-core` or `pouchdb-node`, whatever local name it is given; PouchDB plugin registration, replication and remote CouchDB URLs opened through PouchDB are part of conforming use, not separate instances. An instance violates when offline data is persisted through anything else: localStorage, raw IndexedDB, idb, idb-keyval, Dexie, localforage, RxDB and similar, including a locally defined class or wrapper that merely happens to be named `PouchDB`. A file that mixes PouchDB with another local persistence mechanism is VIOLATED (all-instances). Files with no local data persistence (e.g. pure network fetching, UI without storage) are NOT_APPLICABLE. Because conformance depends on what the constructor identifier is bound to rather than its spelling, the rule is T3.
